# LLM-BANANA

You are one monkey alone in a room with one armed bomb, and nothing is hidden from
you: you see every colour and reading on it, your hands reach every part of it, and
the defusal manual is open in front of you.

A wrong action detonates it. You die. There is no second attempt.

You are shown the bomb and the manual at the start of every round.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    act(op="cut", position=2)
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth doing, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
BOMB AND MANUAL:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
blue. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | yellow |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | white |
| 4 | green |
| 5 | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The sequence has now shown one red flash and three blue flashes. The light remains blue, so counting is not finished; I will wait for the light to go dark.

